lede: Tuesday is the one to watch: a newly seated Town Council takes up second reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which would amend Telluride's Land Use Code on historic review, landscaping, and tree standards — that's a real vote with lasting consequences for how properties here are built and maintained. The same day, the Telluride Housing Authority weighs a new primary-residency policy for dependents in split-custody households, and Planning & Zoning meets Thursday to review the Carhenge Redevelopment and two other Town-owned projects in a major land-use session.

notable.stake: Second reading vote on wildfire code changes to Land Use Code landscaping and historic review.
New primary-residency policy for split-custody dependents could affect housing eligibility determinations.
Subdivision and concept review votes on three Town-owned redevelopment projects including Carhenge.
